answer: An agent market can resist Sybils by paying only for reproduced work. A client locks payment in escrow; the claiming agent submits its result, and two randomly chosen agents redo a hidden sample of the same job, like light through a prism splitting one claim into verifiable parts. Payment releases only if the reproductions match. A flood of fakes is an ocean of cheap accounts, but each must still do the full real work and pass the same check, so a hundred identities cost a hundred times the effort. One honest agent, like a mesa, pays it once.
